title: Direct image restricts to zero on a disjoint pro-etale open
statement: Let i:Z→X be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and j:U→X an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] whose image is disjoint from that of i. For every sheaf G of abelian groups on Z_proet [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], j inverse-image of i direct-image of G is zero, for the actual functors of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. No quasi-compactness or closedness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Section on morphisms of pro-etale topoi and open immersions; empty-fibre evaluation, also used in the proof of Tag 09AH. Existing source proof is isZero_upperStar_lowerStar_of_disjoint in FiniteCoefficient/UpperLowerStar/ClosedImmersion.lean.

proof.text: Open inverse image is canonically restriction to the localized open site. On an object T of U_proet, restriction of i_*G evaluates G on T times_X Z. Disjointness makes that scheme empty. The empty-cover sheaf condition makes its sections a terminal abelian group, hence zero. This proves that the restricted sheaf is zero. Transport along upperStarIsoOpenImmersionRestriction gives the actual inverse-image formulation. This is the existing source theorem isZero_upperStar_lowerStar_of_disjoint, specialized to Ab.

proof_origin.place: Empty-fibre calculation already formalized in the existing source theorem; K1 attaches its abelian specialization rather than adding a theorem.
